why_ai: Claims, denials and posting are rule-bound screen work that AI-native revenue cycle software targets directly.
why_clarity: A claim is paid or denied, with codified payer rules across thousands of near-identical claims.
why_digital: Claims, remittances and EHR data are worked entirely on screen, often for remote clients.

why_ai: Behavioral health denial patterns are highly predictable, so specialty billing automates like general billing.
why_clarity: Distinct code sets and authorisation rules are codified and repeat across sessions.
why_digital: EHR notes, claims and authorisations are handled entirely on screen.

why_ai: Thin contributed benchmarks and pricing guidance are easily replicated from platform data.
why_clarity: Collection rate and days in AR follow standard definitions repeated annually.
why_digital: Contributed operating data in, benchmark reports out, all online.

why_ai: Federal contracts mandate accountable clinical review determinations that providers can appeal.
why_clarity: Medical review follows coverage rules at volume, though determinations are appealed.
why_digital: Claims and records are reviewed on screen under federal contracts.

why_ai: Audit defence under privilege needs certified, accountable reviewers providers trust, though record review automates.
why_clarity: Coding is checked against documentation rules, though audit outcomes take months.
why_digital: Medical records and claims are audited remotely and findings delivered as reports.

why_ai: Credential demand falls as coding automates, though the body controls the recognised credential.
why_clarity: Exams follow defined competency frameworks, but certification never checks coding quality on the job.
why_digital: Content and exams are produced digitally, with some proctored test centres.

why_ai: Denial prediction and appeal generation software competes with AI-native revenue cycle tools.
why_clarity: Denials overturned and prevented are measured against remittance outcomes.
why_digital: Claim and remittance data in, scores and appeal letters out, as software.

why_ai: Most denials are preventable and appeal letters are a direct language model target.
why_clarity: Each denial has a reason code and either pays on resubmission or not.
why_digital: ERA codes, claims and appeal letters are worked entirely on screen.

why_ai: CMN tracking and rental period calculations are rule-based workflows ripe for automation.
why_clarity: HCPCS rules and rental periods are deterministic and repeat on every order.
why_digital: Paper CMNs and faxed authorisations feed screen-based billing.

why_ai: Claim routing and edits are automated, but connectivity to every payer is a durable network.
why_clarity: Claims pass edits and are accepted by payers or rejected instantly.
why_digital: Electronic claims and remittances route entirely between systems.

why_ai: Untrained staff doing billing are the easiest case for guided automation inside the PM system.
why_clarity: Claims pay or deny, but staff learned on the job without a consistent method.
why_digital: Billing runs in the practice's PM system by in-house staff.

why_ai: Clients hire one certified coder for undocumented specialty and payer knowledge.
why_clarity: Coding guidance is checkable against rules, but each question is specialty-specific.
why_digital: Documentation review and guidance delivered remotely.

why_ai: Advisers broker private deals through owner relationships and negotiation.
why_clarity: Each transaction is bespoke and whether value was maximised is never known.
why_digital: Valuations are produced on screen, with deals run through national relationships.

why_ai: The code set is a licensed national standard with no substitute, revised by expert panels.
why_clarity: Annual revisions follow a defined editorial process with fixed effective dates.
why_digital: Code sets and guidance are maintained and licensed digitally.

why_ai: Codifying specialty coding knowledge so any coder can work any client is a direct ML target.
why_clarity: Specialty rules are codified in LCDs and modifiers and claims pay or deny.
why_digital: Claims for remote provider clients are worked entirely on screen.

why_ai: Medical necessity denials and appeal determinations require licensed clinicians and are adversarial.
why_clarity: Edit rules apply at massive volume, though appeals contest the determinations.
why_digital: Claims, edits and appeals are processed entirely in payer systems.

why_ai: High-volume rules-based posting of 835 remittances is ideal automation.
why_clarity: Each payment posts to the right claim and balances exactly or it does not.
why_digital: Electronic remittances are matched to claims entirely on screen.

why_ai: Embedded encounter-to-payment data is durable, though analytics on it automate.
why_clarity: Charge capture and claim outcomes are measured on every encounter.
why_digital: Documentation, charges and claims flow entirely in software.

why_ai: Normalising public rate files is data engineering that AI accelerates and competitors can copy.
why_clarity: Rates are normalised to standard codes across monthly file cycles.
why_digital: Public machine-readable files in, normalised rate data out.

why_ai: Denial and yield analysis over claims data is exactly what ML models do.
why_clarity: Denial rates and collections are measured across huge claim volumes.
why_digital: Claims and remittances analysed entirely in platform software.

why_ai: Deep specialty rules make denial patterns predictable once codified into software.
why_clarity: Specialty coding rules are precise and recur on every claim.
why_digital: Claims and payer rules are worked entirely on screen.

why_ai: Solo billers serve small practices on personal trust, but their manual work is the easiest to automate.
why_clarity: Claims pay or deny, though one-person shops follow their own methods.
why_digital: Paper superbills and clearinghouse portals, serving nearby small practices.
